item: Mississippi Senate: Democrat Scott Colom leads Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith by 28 votes (462,779 to 462,751, 48.9% each) in an unofficial count shortly after midnight Central; AP has not called the race.
source: msindy.org (as of 12:05 AM CT); VoteHub

item: Kansas governor's race too close to call: Democrat Cindy Holscher 546,523 votes, Republican Ty Masterson 540,651, with nearly all precincts counted; AP has not declared a winner.
source: Kansas Secretary of State via Johnson County Post; Kansas Reflector

item: Michigan Senate: Democrat Abdul El-Sayed 51.2%, Republican Mike Rogers 46.9% with an estimated 72% counted; no AP or network call confirmed in this check.
source: DDHQ race update, 1:12 AM ET

item: Nebraska Gov. Jim Pillen (R) declares victory over Democrat Lynne Walz; no AP or network call confirmed in this check.
source: Daily Nebraskan live updates; Nebraska Public Media

item: AP calls New Hampshire's governor race for Republican Gov. Kelly Ayotte over Democrat Cinde Warmington, joining Fox News. Ayotte 51.1%, Warmington 47.3% as of 12:42 AM.
source: Washington Examiner (citing AP), 12:48 AM ET; Fox News

item: Mississippi Senate remains too close to call: Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith 49.7%, Democrat Scott Colom 48.2% with 94% of votes counted.
source: Commercial Dispatch (Columbus, Miss.)

item: Alaska Senate early returns: Democrat Mary Peltola 54.1%, Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan 42.8%, with 45 of 401 precincts reporting; the state will keep accepting ballots for days. Nevada still has not reported any votes in the governor's race.
source: Alaska Division of Elections via Anchorage Daily News, Alaska Beacon; NBC News, CNN results pages

item: Democrat Troy Jackson defeats Sen. Susan Collins in Maine's Senate race, per NBC News; NPR and the Washington Post also report Jackson won (AP call). Collins had conceded earlier.
source: NBC News live blog; NPR; Washington Post

item: CBS News projects Gov. Tina Kotek wins Oregon's governor race over Republican Christine Drazan, joining DDHQ.
source: CBS News via KOIN; DDHQ

item: AP calls governor races for Republicans Mike Mazzei (Oklahoma), Alan Wilson (South Carolina), Phil Scott (Vermont) and Brad Little (Idaho).
source: AP race-call stories via WTOP, Yahoo News, CJME

item: Sen. Susan Collins concedes Maine's Senate race to Democrat Troy Jackson; AP had not called the race as of ~12:30 AM. Jackson 53.0%, Collins 45.82% with 67% in.
source: Maine Morning Star via NENC; DDHQ results page (12:18 AM)

item: AP calls Minnesota's governor race for Democrat Amy Klobuchar over Republican Lisa Demuth; NBC News also reports Klobuchar won.
source: AP via WBTV; NBC News

item: AP calls Maine's governor race for Democrat Hannah Pingree, joining DDHQ; Republican Bobby Charles and independent Rick Bennett conceded.
source: AP via Yahoo News; WGME

item: AP calls Alabama's open Senate seat for Republican Barry Moore over Democrat Everett Wess.
source: AP via Yahoo News

item: CBS News projects Democrat Gina Hinojosa defeats Gov. Greg Abbott in Texas, joining NBC News; shown as won here.
source: CBS News Texas; NBC News

item: Fox News Decision Desk projects Republican Gov. Kelly Ayotte wins New Hampshire's governor race over Democrat Cinde Warmington; awaiting a second call.
source: Fox News

item: AP calls Minnesota's Senate race for Democrat Peggy Flanagan (54.36%, 70.6% counted) and Hawaii's governor race for Gov. Josh Green; NBC News projects both. NBC's Senate tally stands at 52 Democrats, 41 Republicans, 7 uncalled, with NBC and CNBC projecting Democratic control of both chambers.
source: AP via Washington Examiner, CKOM; NBC News results page and live blog; CNBC

item: AP calls Iowa's Senate race for Democrat Josh Turek over Republican Ashley Hinson; NBC News also projects Turek, joining DDHQ.
source: Iowa Capital Dispatch (AP); NBC News results page; DDHQ

item: AP calls Oregon's Senate race for Democratic Sen. Jeff Merkley over Republican David Brock Smith, joining Fox News (initial statewide results 57.06% to 40.24%).
source: Banks Post (AP); Fox News

item: AP calls South Dakota's governor race for Republican Gov. Larry Rhoden over Democrat Dan Ahlers.
source: KOTA-TV (AP)

item: Mississippi Senate: Democrat Scott Colom leads Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith 49.1% to 48.8% with an estimated 87% in; not called.
source: DDHQ

item: Not race calls: Republican Tommy Tuberville (Alabama governor) and Republican Marsha Blackburn (Tennessee governor) declared victory; AP had not called Alabama as of ~11:30 PM ET, and no call was reported in Tennessee. DDHQ projects Gov. Tina Kotek wins Oregon's governor race; awaiting a second call.
source: WSFA; WVLT; That Oregon Life (DDHQ)

item: NBC News projects Democrats win control of the U.S. Senate, in addition to the House. CNBC also reports Democrats have flipped the Senate.
source: NBC News live blog and Senate results page; CNBC

item: AP calls Ohio's special Senate election for Democrat Sherrod Brown over Republican Sen. Jon Husted (Brown 48.6%, Husted 46.5% at the call); NBC News also projects Brown.
source: AP via Local 12 (WKRC); NBC News results page

item: AP calls Iowa's governor race for Democrat Rob Sand over Republican Zach Lahn (Sand 57.7%, Lahn 42.3%, 79% counted); CBS News and DDHQ also project Sand.
source: AP via Washington Examiner; CBS News; DDHQ

item: AP calls Kansas's Senate race for Democrat Adam Hamilton over Republican Sen. Roger Marshall, joining DDHQ; shown as won here. AP also calls Arkansas's Senate race for Republican Sen. Tom Cotton, joining Fox News.
source: AP via KSHB and KATV; DDHQ; Fox News

item: CBS News and DDHQ project Democratic Gov. Katie Hobbs wins Arizona's governor race over Republican Andy Biggs; shown as won here.
source: CBS News and DDHQ via KTAR, azfamily

item: DDHQ projects Democrat Josh Turek wins Iowa's Senate race over Republican Ashley Hinson; awaiting a second call.
source: DDHQ via The Hill

item: NBC News projects Democrat Gina Hinojosa wins Texas's governor race over Gov. Greg Abbott (57% to 41.7% with 67% counted as of 11:17 PM); awaiting a second call. An ABC7 Amarillo headline reports Abbott conceded.
source: NBC News results page; Washington Examiner; ABC7 Amarillo

item: Concessions (not race calls): in Maine's governor race, Republican Bobby Charles and independent Rick Bennett conceded to Democrat Hannah Pingree; in South Carolina, Democrat Jermaine Johnson conceded to Republican Alan Wilson.
source: Portland Press Herald; SC Daily Gazette
